messages:
elena-sec: Heads-up — during the quarterly access sweep I found a service account in prod-project-b with cross-project KMS decrypt on key projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/etl/cryptoKeys/etl-key. No owner listed in the console. Can @samir-eng take a quick look and confirm why it exists? Ticket INC-4521 https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4521

samir-eng: On it. Running an IAM audit now. quick commands: `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy analytics-worker@prod-project-b.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and `gcloud projects get-iam-policy prod-project-b --flatten='bindings[]' --format='table(bindings.role,bindings.members)'`

leah-ops: FYI the ETL team historically used a shared svcacct for batch decrypts. We rotated keys last year but the SA likely predates that. If it's used we should see activity in Cloud Audit Logs > dataAccess for cryptoKey.decrypt.

marta-auditor: Can we pull a short audit query for grant events and decryption calls? Suggest Log Explorer filter: `resource.type="crypto_key" protoPayload.methodName:("Decrypt" "SetIamPolicy" )` and narrow to the SA email. Need time window of last 90 days.

infra-bot: Automated check: found 2 principals with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on key projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/etl/cryptoKeys/etl-key — members: serviceAccount:analytics-worker@prod-project-b.iam.gserviceaccount.com, projectEditor:proj-editor@redwood-prod. Timestamp: 2025-11-02T15:22:10Z

samir-eng: Quick findings: the SA was created and bound by terraform module `modules/etl/kms.tf` on 2025-11-02 (see infra repo commit d4c3a1). I ran a logs check — there were decrypt calls from the SA between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-01, then nothing after. No current owners in the service desk ticket.

elena-sec: Thanks. Proposed path: 1) Open a short owner discovery ping to the ETL slack channel (7d response window). 2) Add a scoped canary role removal for non-prod first. 3) If no owner/usage after 7d, revoke decrypt binding from the SA and monitor app fallout for 24h, rollback if errors. Is that acceptable?

leah-ops: I'm +1. For the revoke step use: ```gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/etl/cryptoKeys/etl-key --member='serviceAccount:analytics-worker@prod-project-b.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'``` Do it during a low-traffic window and have a rollback command ready: ```gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ...```

marta-auditor: Also add an evidence artifact to INC-4521 with the logs query results and terraform commit link. I'll tag compliance for the record.

samir-eng: I'll send the owner ping now and attach the `terraform` commit and last-use logs. If no reply by 7d I'll create the IAM change request and run the revoke canary in staging.

elena-sec: Great. @deploy-bot please create a follow-up reminder in 7 days and add INC-4521 to the access-review board agenda.

deploy-bot: Reminder created: INC-4521 — Access sweep follow-up (owner discovery for analytics-worker SA). Due in 7 days. Assigned: samir-eng. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Post-action note: if revoke happens, run this post-check: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=crypto_key AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=analytics-worker@prod-project-b.iam.gserviceaccount.com AND protoPayload.methodName:Decrypt" --freshness=24h` to validate no sudden errors.

elena-sec: Perfect. I'll draft the short playbook steps and paste them into the ticket. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
